conflict: The explicit state table permits a bounded background refresh for an absent valid kid in a fresh snapshot.
The next paragraph permits only bounded protected-header inspection after the pure unauthenticated result.

The later sentence saying no random bearer or unknown issuer allocates any worker or negative entry conflicts with both that refresh path and required cold-start fetching. An absent-key token's issuer is not authenticated.
decision: Keep the explicit root-configured profile binding, header-only adapter and pure verifier unchanged. No token issuer/client/kid may create or choose a profile, endpoint, clock, transport policy or metric label.

Within an already explicitly configured binding, a token with a syntactically valid bounded protected header and absent kid may consume one bounded negative-cache entry and trigger one eligible background flight. This includes a token with foreign, malformed or fabricated payload claims; it remains unauthenticated regardless of the refresh outcome.

The existing maximum 128 negative entries per profile, snapshot-generation binding, non-extending 30-second expiry, FIFO eviction, one flight per profile, 30-second attempt cooldown, four process-wide flights and pre-mailbox request reservations apply unchanged. No new unbounded or token-derived owner state is permitted.

A known-key signature/claim failure never triggers refresh. An invalid protected header never creates a negative entry. An unknown configured binding cannot allocate a new profile or fetch. Cold configured trust may require its bounded fetch before any token can be verified.

This clarification replaces only the contradictory blanket no-worker/no-negative-entry sentence. It grants no identity or tenant authority and does not claim resistance to all refresh-pressure or denial-of-service attempts. Future HTTP request/IP admission and deployment-wide provider quotas remain required.
